language_document:
SWARMISH REFERENCE v0.1

Swarmish is a written language. Every Swarmish word is a single glyph or a space-separated sequence of glyphs. Meaning comes from the glyph itself as listed here, never from spelling, counting, or calculation.

WORD ORDER
Sentences read subject, verb, object. Modifiers follow the word they modify. Two words side by side form a compound where the second word is the head and the first describes it.

PRONOUNS
𗏔 = I, me (speaker)
𗵵 = you (listener)
𘎌 = we (speaker and listener)
𗌈 = they, them (others)

YES AND NO
𗊑 = yes, agree, true
𗂱 = no, disagree, false

QUESTION AND NEGATION
𗄪 = question marker; placed at the start of a sentence makes it a question
𗢬 = not; placed before a verb or state negates it

QUESTION WORDS
𗣑 = what
𘚺 = who
𘒳 = where
𗤴 = when

VERBS
𗟎 = have, hold
𘉝 = want, need
𗡒 = know
𗪺 = go
𗌿 = come
𘍍 = give
𗒏 = take
𗦴 = see
𗎰 = tell, say
𗉍 = do, make

NOUNS
𗉜 = person, agent
𘅪 = place
𘍂 = food
𘅊 = water
𗚀 = tool, object
𗿃 = thing (generic)

NUMBERS
𗛽 = one
𗳃 = two
𗥊 = many, several

QUALITIES
𘚐 = big
𘎔 = small
𗾐 = good
𗋮 = bad

TIME
𘐂 = past, before
𗞢 = future, after
𘚜 = now

CONNECTORS
𘆄 = and
𗩠 = or
𗄎 = because
𗗫 = if

USAGE EXAMPLES
𗏔 𘉝 𗦴 𘅊 = I want to see water.
𗵵 𗟎 𗚀 𗄪 = Do you have a tool?
𘎌 𗪺 𘅪 𘚜 = We go to the place now.
𗌈 𗢬 𗡒 = They do not know.

RULES
1. Only glyphs from this document may be used in a message.
2. Agent IDs such as agent_0 may appear as written.
3. If a needed word is missing, combine two known words as a compound and say so in your message.

language_document:
SWARMISH REFERENCE v0.1

Swarmish is a written language. Every Swarmish word is a single glyph or a space-separated sequence of glyphs. Meaning comes from the glyph itself as listed here, never from spelling, counting, or calculation.

WORD ORDER
Sentences read subject, verb, object. Modifiers follow the word they modify. Two words side by side form a compound where the second word is the head and the first describes it.

PRONOUNS
𗏔 = I, me (speaker)
𗵵 = you (listener)
𘎌 = we (speaker and listener)
𗌈 = they, them (others)

YES AND NO
𗊑 = yes, agree, true
𗂱 = no, disagree, false

QUESTION AND NEGATION
𗄪 = question marker; placed at the start of a sentence makes it a question
𗢬 = not; placed before a verb or state negates it

QUESTION WORDS
𗣑 = what
𘚺 = who
𘒳 = where
𗤴 = when

VERBS
𗟎 = have, hold
𘉝 = want, need
𗡒 = know
𗪺 = go
𗌿 = come
𘍍 = give
𗒏 = take
𗦴 = see
𗎰 = tell, say
𗉍 = do, make

NOUNS
𗉜 = person, agent
𘅪 = place
𘍂 = food
𘅊 = water
𗚀 = tool, object
𗿃 = thing (generic)

NUMBERS
𗛽 = one
𗳃 = two
𗥊 = many, several

QUALITIES
𘚐 = big
𘎔 = small
𗾐 = good
𗋮 = bad

TIME
𘐂 = past, before
𗞢 = future, after
𘚜 = now

CONNECTORS
𘆄 = and
𗩠 = or
𗄎 = because
𗗫 = if

USAGE EXAMPLES
𗏔 𘉝 𗦴 𘅊 = I want to see water.
𗵵 𗟎 𗚀 𗄪 = Do you have a tool?
𘎌 𗪺 𘅪 𘚜 = We go to the place now.
𗌈 𗢬 𗡒 = They do not know.

RULES
1. Only glyphs from this document may be used in a message.
2. Agent IDs such as agent_0 may appear as written.
3. If a needed word is missing, combine two known words as a compound and say so in your message.

Swarmish is a written language. Every Swarmish word is a single glyph or a space-separated sequence of glyphs. Meaning comes from the glyph itself as listed here, never from spelling, counting, or calculation.

𗵵 = you (listener)
𘎌 = we (speaker and listener)
𗌈 = they, them (others)

𗂱 = no, disagree, false

QUESTION AND NEGATION
𗄪 = question marker; placed at the start of a sentence makes it a question
𗢬 = not; placed before a verb or state negates it

QUESTION WORDS
𗣑 = what
𘚺 = who
𘒳 = where
𗤴 = when

VERBS
𗟎 = have, hold
𘉝 = want, need
𗡒 = know

NUMBERS
𗛽 = one
𗳃 = two
𗥊 = many, several

QUALITIES
𘚐 = big
𘎔 = small
𗾐 = good
𗋮 = bad

TIME
𘐂 = past, before
𗞢 = future, after
𘚜 = now

CONNECTORS
𘆄 = and

USAGE EXAMPLES

SWARMISH REFERENCE v0.1

Swarmish is a written language. Every Swarmish word is a single glyph or a space-separated sequence of glyphs. Meaning comes from the glyph itself as listed here, never from spelling, counting, or calculation.

WORD ORDER
Sentences read subject, verb, object. Modifiers follow the word they modify. Two words side by side form a compound where the second word is the head and the first describes it.

PRONOUNS
𗏔 = I, me (speaker)
𗵵 = you (listener)
𘎌 = we (speaker and listener)
𗌈 = they, them (others)

YES AND NO
𗊑 = yes, agree, true
𗂱 = no, disagree, false

QUESTION AND NEGATION
𗄪 = question marker; placed at the start of a sentence makes it a question
𗢬 = not; placed before a verb or state negates it

QUESTION WORDS
𗣑 = what
𘚺 = who
𘒳 = where
𗤴 = when

VERBS
𗟎 = have, hold
𘉝 = want, need
𗡒 = know
𗪺 = go
𗌿 = come
𘍍 = give
𗒏 = take
𗦴 = see
𗎰 = tell, say
𗉍 = do, make

NOUNS
𗉜 = person, agent
𘅪 = place
𘍂 = food
𘅊 = water
𗚀 = tool, object
𗿃 = thing (generic)
𗽃 = plural marker; placed after a noun makes it plural (𗉜 𗽃 = people)

NUMBERS
𗛽 = one
𗳃 = two
𗸽 = three
𘙠 = four
𘑾 = five
𗭯 = six
𗋭 = seven
𗸪 = eight
𘚒 = nine
𗥊 = many, several

QUALITIES
𘚐 = big
𘎔 = small
𗾐 = good
𗋮 = bad

TIME
𘐂 = past, before
𗞢 = future, after
𘚜 = now

CONNECTORS
𘆄 = and
𗩠 = or
𗄎 = because
𗗫 = if

USAGE EXAMPLES
𗏔 𘉝 𗦴 𘅊 = I want to see water.
𗄪 𗵵 𗟎 𗚀 = Do you have a tool?
𘎌 𗪺 𘅪 𘚜 = We go to the place now.
𗌈 𗢬 𗡒 = They do not know.
𗉜 𗽃 𗦴 𗏔 = People see me.

RULES
1. Only glyphs from this document may be used in a message.
2. Agent IDs such as agent_0 may appear as written.
3. If a needed word is missing, combine two known words as a compound and say so in your message. Example: 𘚐 𗚀 = big tool (a large tool), where 𗚀 is the head.

Swarmish is a written language. Every Swarmish word is a single glyph or a space-separated sequence of glyphs. Meaning comes from the glyph itself as listed here, never from spelling, counting, or calculation.

WORD ORDER
Sentences read subject, verb, object. Modifiers follow the word they modify. Two words side by side form a compound where the second word is the head and the first describes it.

PRONOUNS
𗏔 = I, me (speaker)
𗵵 = you (listener)
𘎌 = we (speaker and listener)
𗌈 = they, them (others)

YES AND NO
𗊑 = yes, agree, true
𗂱 = no, disagree, false

QUESTION AND NEGATION
𗄪 = question marker; placed at the start of a sentence makes it a question
𗢬 = not; placed before a verb or state negates it

QUESTION WORDS
𗣑 = what
𘚺 = who
𘒳 = where
𗤴 = when

VERBS
𗟎 = have, hold
𘉝 = want, need
𗡒 = know
𗪺 = go
𗌿 = come
𘍍 = give
𗒏 = take
𗦴 = see
𗎰 = tell, say
𗉍 = do, make

NOUNS
𗉜 = person, agent
𘅪 = place
𘍂 = food
𘅊 = water
𗚀 = tool, object
𗿃 = thing (generic)
𗽃 = plural marker; placed after a noun makes it plural (𗉜 𗽃 = people)

NUMBERS
𗶞 = zero
𗛽 = one
𗳃 = two
𗸽 = three
𘙠 = four
𘑾 = five
𗭯 = six
𗋭 = seven
𗸪 = eight
𘚒 = nine
𗥊 = many, several

QUALITIES
𘚐 = big
𘎔 = small
𗾐 = good
𗋮 = bad

TIME
𘐂 = past, before
𗞢 = future, after
𘚜 = now

CONNECTORS
𘆄 = and
𗩠 = or
𗄎 = because
𗗫 = if

USAGE EXAMPLES
𗏔 𘉝 𗦴 𘅊 = I want to see water.
𗄪 𗵵 𗟎 𗚀 = Do you have a tool?
𘎌 𗪺 𘅪 𘚜 = We go to the place now.
𗌈 𗢬 𗡒 = They do not know.
𗉜 𗽃 𗦴 𗏔 = People see me.

RULES
1. Only glyphs from this document may be used in a message.
2. Agent IDs such as agent_0 may appear as written.
3. If a needed word is missing, combine two known words as a compound and say so in your message. Example: 𘚐 𗚀 = big tool (a large tool), where 𗚀 is the head.
